title: Differentials of A[x]/(x^p - a) in characteristic p
statement: Let $p$ be a prime, $A$ a commutative ring with $p\cdot1_A=0$ (an $\mathbf F_p$-algebra), $a_1,\dots,a_n\in A$, and $A'=A[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(x_1^p-a_1,\dots,x_n^p-a_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $\Omega$, $\mathrm d$ be as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Then: (1) $\Omega_{A'/A}$ is a free $A'$-module with basis $\mathrm dx_1,\dots,\mathrm dx_n$ (images of the variables); (2) the sequence of $A'$-modules $$A'^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon\ }A'\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{\ w\ }\Omega_{A'/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{\ z\ }\Omega_{A'/A}\to0,$$ with $\varepsilon(e_j)=1\otimes\mathrm da_j$, $w(c\otimes\mathrm da)=c\,\mathrm d(a\cdot1_{A'})$ and $z(c\,\mathrm dc')=c\,\mathrm dc'$, is exact.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07E5, (2) => (4) (lines 8785-8825): 'By Algebra, Lemma 00S4 we see that NL_{A'/A} is homotopy equivalent to ... zero differential, i.e. H_1(L_{A'/A}) and Omega_{A'/A} are free of rank n. The Jacobi-Zariski sequence for F_p -> A -> A' ... the jth basis vector of H_1(L_{A'/A}) maps to da_j (x) 1'; tags 00S4 (algebra-lemma-change-base-NL) and 00S2 verified in stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: *Notation; $\mathrm d f_j=0$.* Let $P=A[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $f_j=x_j^p-a_j\in P$ ($a_j$ meaning $a_j\cdot1_P$), $I=(f_1,\dots,f_n)\subseteq P$, and $\alpha:P\to A'=P/I$ the quotient map; write $\bar x_i=\alpha(x_i)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis] $\Omega_{P/A}$ is free on $\mathrm dx_1,\dots,\mathrm dx_n$ and $\mathrm df_j=\sum_k\frac{\partial f_j}{\partial x_k}\mathrm dx_k=p\,x_j^{p-1}\,\mathrm dx_j=0$, because $\partial a_j/\partial x_k=0$ ($a_j$ is a constant) and $p\cdot1_A=0$. Consequently, for every $g\in I$, written $g=\sum_jh_jf_j$ with $h_j\in P$, the Leibniz rule [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] gives $\mathrm dg=\sum_j(h_j\,\mathrm df_j+f_j\,\mathrm dh_j)=\sum_jf_j\,\mathrm dh_j$, hence $1\otimes\mathrm dg=\sum_j\alpha(f_j)\otimes\mathrm dh_j=0$ in $A'\otimes_P\Omega_{P/A}$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition 07E5 (more-algebra-proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular), (2) => (4), lines 8785-8825 ('d(x_j^p - a_j) = 0 in Omega_{k[x_1,...,x_n]/k}')

proof.text: *Proof of (1).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] to $A\to P$ and the ideal $\mathfrak a=I$, so $C=P/I=A'$: the sequence $I/I^2\xrightarrow{\delta}A'\otimes_P\Omega_{P/A}\xrightarrow{w_0}\Omega_{A'/A}\to0$, $\delta(g\bmod I^2)=1\otimes\mathrm dg$, $w_0(c\otimes\mathrm dq)=c\,\mathrm d\alpha(q)$, is exact. By step 1, $\delta=0$, so $w_0$ is injective and surjective, an isomorphism of $A'$-modules, with $w_0(1\otimes\mathrm dx_i)=\mathrm d\bar x_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] (with $T=\{1,\dots,n\}$ and the $P$-algebra $S=A'$) the $A'$-module $A'\otimes_P\Omega_{P/A}$ is free with basis $1\otimes\mathrm dx_1,\dots,1\otimes\mathrm dx_n$. An isomorphism carries a basis to a basis, so $\Omega_{A'/A}$ is free with basis $\mathrm d\bar x_1,\dots,\mathrm d\bar x_n$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition 07E5 (more-algebra-proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular), (2) => (4), lines 8785-8825 ('NL_{A'/A} is homotopy equivalent to the complex ... with the zero differential, i.e. ... Omega_{A'/A} [is] free of rank n')

proof.text: *$H_1$ of the presentation $\alpha$.* The map $\alpha:P\to A'$ is a presentation of $A'$ over $A$ in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality], with naive cotangent complex $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha):I/I^2\xrightarrow{\mathrm d_\alpha}A'\otimes_P\Omega_{P/A}$, $\mathrm d_\alpha(g\bmod I^2)=1\otimes\mathrm dg$. By step 1, $\mathrm d_\alpha=0$, so $H_1(\mathrm{NL}(\alpha))=\ker\mathrm d_\alpha=I/I^2$. As an $A'$-module it is generated by $f_1\bmod I^2,\dots,f_n\bmod I^2$: for $g=\sum_jh_jf_j\in I$ one has $g\bmod I^2=\sum_j\alpha(h_j)\cdot(f_j\bmod I^2)$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition 07E5 (more-algebra-proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular), (2) => (4), lines 8785-8825 ('Using the presentation A[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A' with kernel (x_j^p - a_j)')

proof.text: *Comparison with the canonical presentation.* Let $\gamma:A[A']\to A'$, $[c]\mapsto c$, be the canonical presentation with kernel $I_{A'/A}$, used in [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] to define $\mathrm{NL}_{A'/A}$ and $H_1(L_{A'/A})$. It is a presentation in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality] (a polynomial ring on the set $A'$), and $\mathrm{NL}(\gamma)$ is $\mathrm{NL}_{A'/A}$: by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] $A'\otimes_{A[A']}\Omega_{A[A']/A}$ is free on the $1\otimes\mathrm d[c]$, and under $1\otimes\mathrm d[c]\mapsto\mathrm d[c]$ the map $\mathrm d_\gamma(g\bmod I_{A'/A}^2)=1\otimes\mathrm dg=\sum_c\gamma(\partial g/\partial[c])\otimes\mathrm d[c]$ becomes $\delta$ of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]; so $H_1(\mathrm{NL}(\gamma))=H_1(L_{A'/A})$ as submodules of $I_{A'/A}/I_{A'/A}^2$. Let $\varphi:P\to A[A']$ be the $A$-algebra map with $\varphi(x_i)=[\bar x_i]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; then $\gamma\circ\varphi$ and $\alpha$ are $A$-algebra maps agreeing on the variables, so $\gamma\circ\varphi=\alpha$ and $\varphi$ is a morphism of presentations from $\alpha$ to $\gamma$ over the identity square ($R=R'=A$, $\psi=\mathrm{id}_{A'}$). Choose for every $c\in A'$ some $\sigma(c)\in P$ with $\alpha(\sigma(c))=c$ ($\alpha$ is surjective) and let $\chi:A[A']\to P$ be the $A$-algebra map $[c]\mapsto\sigma(c)$; then $\alpha\circ\chi=\gamma$ (agreement on the variables), so $\chi$ is a morphism of presentations from $\gamma$ to $\alpha$. By clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality], $\chi\circ\varphi$ is a morphism from $\alpha$ to $\alpha$ and $\varphi\circ\chi$ one from $\gamma$ to $\gamma$, with $(\chi\circ\varphi)_*=\chi_*\varphi_*$ and $(\varphi\circ\chi)_*=\varphi_*\chi_*$; by clause (1) they equal $(\mathrm{id}_P)_*$ and $(\mathrm{id}_{A[A']})_*$, which are identities by clause (2). Hence $\varphi_*:H_1(\mathrm{NL}(\alpha))\to H_1(L_{A'/A})$, $g\bmod I^2\mapsto\varphi(g)\bmod I_{A'/A}^2$, is an isomorphism of $A'$-modules. With step 3: $H_1(L_{A'/A})$ is generated as an $A'$-module by the classes $h_j=\varphi(f_j)\bmod I_{A'/A}^2$ of $\varphi(f_j)=[\bar x_j]^p-a_j\in I_{A'/A}$, $j=1,\dots,n$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition 07E5 (more-algebra-proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular), (2) => (4), lines 8785-8825 ('By Algebra, Lemma 00S4 we see that NL_{A'/A} is homotopy equivalent to ...'; here the comparison of the presentation alpha with the canonical one, Algebra 00S1)

proof.text: *The Jacobi-Zariski sequence and the connecting map on $h_j$.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence] to $\mathbf F_p\to A\to A'$ (its $A,B,C$ being $\mathbf F_p,A,A'$): the sequence $H_1(L_{A'/A})\xrightarrow{\partial}A'\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{A'/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{z}\Omega_{A'/A}\to0$ is exact, where $w(c\otimes\mathrm da)=c\,\mathrm d(a\cdot1_{A'})$ and $z(c\,\mathrm dc')=c\,\mathrm dc'$ are exactly the maps $w,z$ of the statement, and $\partial(g\bmod I_{A'/A}^2)=\sum_\alpha\gamma([c]^\alpha)\otimes\mathrm db_\alpha$ for $g=\sum_\alpha b_\alpha[c]^\alpha\in I_{A'/A}$ written in the monomials of $A[A']$ with coefficients $b_\alpha\in A$. For $g=\varphi(f_j)=1\cdot[\bar x_j]^p+(-a_j)\cdot1$ (two distinct monomials, $p\ge2$: $[\bar x_j]^p$ with coefficient $1$ and the constant monomial with coefficient $-a_j$) this gives $\partial(h_j)=\gamma([\bar x_j]^p)\otimes\mathrm d(1)+\gamma(1)\otimes\mathrm d(-a_j)=-1\otimes\mathrm da_j$, since $\mathrm d(1)=0$ and $\mathrm d$ is additive [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. (The source says the $j$-th basis vector maps to $\mathrm da_j\otimes1$; with the sign convention of the cited node it maps to $-\mathrm da_j\otimes1$, which does not change images.)

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition 07E5 (more-algebra-proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular), (2) => (4), lines 8785-8825 ('The Jacobi-Zariski sequence for F_p -> A -> A' is ... unwinding the maps in Algebra, Lemma 00S2, ... the jth basis vector of H_1(L_{A'/A}) maps to da_j (x) 1')

proof.text: *Proof of (2).* $\partial$ is $A'$-linear and $H_1(L_{A'/A})$ is generated by $h_1,\dots,h_n$ (step 4), so by step 5 $\operatorname{im}\partial$ is the $A'$-submodule generated by $-1\otimes\mathrm da_1,\dots,-1\otimes\mathrm da_n$, which is the submodule generated by $1\otimes\mathrm da_1,\dots,1\otimes\mathrm da_n$, i.e. $\operatorname{im}\varepsilon$ for the $A'$-linear map $\varepsilon:A'^{\oplus n}\to A'\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}$, $e_j\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm da_j$. Hence $\ker w=\operatorname{im}\partial=\operatorname{im}\varepsilon$; exactness at $\Omega_{A'/\mathbf F_p}$ and surjectivity of $z$ are part of the exact sequence of step 5. So $A'^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}A'\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{A'/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{z}\Omega_{A'/A}\to0$ is exact.

split_report.summary: Split into 6 steps following More on Algebra 07E5 (2)=>(4) (lines 8785-8825), using only existing nodes, no new node. Step 1: d(x_j^p - a_j) = p x_j^{p-1} dx_j = 0 in Omega_{P/A} (polynomial Kaehler basis leaf), so 1 (x) dg = 0 for g in I. Step 2: clause (1) from the 00RU leaf (jacobi-zariski-differential-maps) with delta = 0 and the base-changed basis of the any-variables Kaehler leaf. Step 3: H_1 of the presentation alpha is I/I^2, generated by the f_j. Step 4: comparison of alpha with the canonical presentation by the 00S1 leaf (nl-presentation-h1-functoriality): phi: x_i -> [x_i] and a section chi give inverse maps on H_1, so H_1(L_{A'/A}) is generated by the classes of [x_j]^p - a_j. Step 5: the Jacobi-Zariski sequence of F_p -> A -> A' (00S2 node, reviewed) with its explicit connecting map gives partial(h_j) = -1 (x) da_j. Step 6: im partial = im epsilon, giving (2). The source's freeness of H_1(L_{A'/A}) (via 00S4, which needs flatness over the field k) is neither stated by the item nor needed (only generation by the f_j is used), so no regular-sequence/Koszul node is needed. Sign: the connecting map sends h_j to -da_j (x) 1, not da_j (x) 1 as the source writes; images agree. The citer lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-h1-injective uses exactly (1) and (2) as stated. Mathlib re-searched (leansearch, loogle, leanfinder, grep, local_search): no match.
